title: Cascading slowpath investigation scratchpad
content:
Goal: quick exploratory notes to triage repeated p99+ slowpath events observed on a small subset of hosts (prod-dedicated pool). Objective is to reproduce in sandbox, isolate root cause (scheduling vs memory pressure vs kernel issue), and propose mitigations (backoff, circuit breaker, mem thresholds).

Background:
- Symptom: intermittent high tail latency (p99.9 spikes to 5–12s) for otherwise short text-generation requests (<=128 tokens). Most requests return ~60–120ms.
- Affected nodes: ~6 hosts out of ~120 in dedicated pool; spikes correlate with simultaneous background GC/sidecar batch loads on those hosts.
- Hypothesis: cascading slowpath — small queue/backpressure + sudden kernel-level stall (GPU page-fault? host OOM killer? process scheduling starvation) causes request execution to fall off fast path into slowpath (sync copies, fallback decode), amplifying queue delays.

Quick observations (raw):
- Short trace excerpt (sampled):
  2026-02-18T14:12:03.041Z GET /v1/generate 200 latency_ms=73
  2026-02-18T14:12:07.118Z GET /v1/generate 504 latency_ms=5034 host=ded-24
  2026-02-18T14:12:07.119Z gpu_mem_free_mb=1024 gpu_mem_total_mb=16384 cpu_load_1m=4.2
  2026-02-18T14:12:07.129Z kernel_wakeup_wait_ms=4123 threads_blocked=9

- Simple table of aggregated runs (sandbox repro attempts):
  run | config | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | p999(ms) | notes
  -----|--------|---------|---------|---------|----------|------
  base | default batching | 78 | 132 | 240 | 520 | no repro
  mem_pressure | +background load (30%) | 84 | 190 | 620 | 4100 | intermittent spikes on 1/20 hosts
  mem_pressure_high | +background load (60%) | 95 | 220 | 1400 | 8700 | consistent spikes, correlates with cuda page-faults in dmesg
  preempt | preemptive process spun | 82 | 150 | 300 | 560 | spikes rare

- dmesg sample on repro host: "[172849.123456] NVRM: Xid (0000:08:00): 79, PID 2345 ..." (seen near p99 events) — suggests GPU driver catching ECC or SMMU faults.

Repro plan (short):
1) Controlled sandbox with 2 replica processes on same host to emulate tenant co-location. Use tiny generator load (qps=15) + background stress (tensor-concat job) to raise GPU memory churn.
2) Enable verbose driver + perf counters collection (nvidia-smi dmon, nsys capture) around spike window.
3) Run 12-hour sweep with randomized background jobs to capture rare events.
4) Add instrumentation in runtime to log 'slowpath entry reason' (kvcache miss + fallback decode + sync-copy indicator).

Quick instrumentation additions (notes to self):
- Add per-request tag: fastpath=true/false, reason=[kvcache-miss|preemption|mem-copy-fallback|kernel-wake] and emit metric counter.
- Sample stack traces for requests > 1s inside runtime and attach to telemetry bundle. Keep sampling rate low (1/1000) to limit overhead.

Commands used (sandbox):
- stress load (toy): ./bg_tensor_loop --alloc-pattern=fragmented --mem-alloc=6G --interval-ms=200
- short client run: hey -n 20000 -c 40 -m POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":64}'
- capture: nsys profile --output=nsys_run --sample=cpu --trace=cuda --duration=240s --pid=2345

Initial findings (so far):
- When GPU memory churn is high and there are frequent small host allocations, latency tails rise sharply. Kernel logs show repeated page-fault/eviction/reclaim messages; these align with p99.9 windows.
- Some spikes show a long 'kernel_wakeup_wait_ms' recorded in our runtime (thread waiting on host condvar after requesting CUDA stream synchronization) — indicates blocking at host synchronization boundary rather than pure network/carrier queueing.
- Not all nodes with high churn show spikes — seems correlated with specific driver/firmware combo (checked using nvidia-smi -q). Might be reproducible only with older driver stacks.

Short-term mitigations to try (experiments):
- Conservative mem-reservation: pin a fixed 1–2GB GPU reserved pool for runtime so background tenant allocation cannot fully fragment top-of-memory, test p99 behavior.
- Try single-process multi-thread vs multi-process worker layout — processes might suffer more from OS-level preemption when under memory pressure.
- Add coalescing backoff: when slowpath counter crosses threshold, temporarily reduce new-batch sizes and increase async-prefetch window to avoid sync-copy fallback.
- Driver/firmware upgrade on one canary host to see if spikes disappear.

Longer-term questions / open items:
- Can we detect imminent kernel-level stalls before they manifest in latency? (perf counters + small probe kernel?)
- Is this a vendor driver bug vs workload anti-pattern (lots of small cold allocations)? Need to partner with infra and file vendor ticket if driver traces match known issues.
- Should we expose a "memory headroom" SLO per tenant (recommendation in Dedicated offering) and enforce via admission control?

Notes for next sync with Rhea/Kai (agenda):
- Show nsys capture trace and dmesg excerpts (attach to JIRA-8342).
- Decide on a canary upgrade (driver) and a runtime flag for mem-reservation (a quick runtime patch exists: mem_reserve_mb).
- Agree on signal to use for automatic batch-backoff (suggest: >3 slowpath hits in 30s on host).

Misc scratch TODOs:
- [ ] Add telemetry tag to all slowpath events (done: preliminary)
- [ ] Run 24h randomized sweep and collect ~50GB of traces (estimate)
- [ ] Reproduce with driver v535 and v555 (record results)
- [ ] Draft short runbook for oncall if slowpath spikes escalate (include pod drainage recipe)

Quick conclusion (working):
- Likely multi-factor: memory churn + driver-level page-fault/eviction path causing host-level blocking, amplified by request batching and kvcache misses. Priority: reproduce reliably in sandbox and test driver upgrade + mem-reservation.

End of notes.

(These are personal working notes — rough, incomplete, and intentionally informal.)
